subject: Testing the significance of factor loadings

messages.author: 9403604069d4685f
messages.subject: Testing the significance of factor loadings
parts:
Hi,

In some articles I can see that the authors have performed IRT and listed factor loadings of the items (presumably the ones you get after you add
@Fit
to the fitted mirt object in R. However, those authors also say that they have tested the significance of the loadings, which are all under .001. I am wondering is it possible to do this in mirt?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Testing the significance of factor loadings
parts:
It seems a little silly to do this. The significance of the factor loadings is really the same as the significance of the slope parameters. They become slightly different if you are testing a value other than 0, in which case applying the delta method is possible but still not very recommended (I've written about this in a paper that studied profile-likelihood CIs, and these functions incidentally ended up into the function PLCI.mirt()). I would probably just report the significance of the raw slope parameters instead since this implies the significance of the loadings. HTH.

Phil
